dossier.scp_unleashed.012.title: A Bad Composition
dossier.scp_unleashed.012.caption: SCP-012 at intake, laid beside the case it arrived in.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-012 is to be kept in a storage container with a solid door, and the door is to stay shut. **No glass front is ever to be fitted to its container.** Behind a shut, solid door SCP-012 is inert.
SCP-012 is never to be carried in the hand, and no member of staff is to touch it. Outside its container it is kept only inside a sealed containment case.
Personnel are not to hold SCP-012 in either hand, or look at it through glass or an open door from within 8 m. Any further copies of SCP-012 are to be cased and stored in the same way.
Personnel designated SCP-012-2 are to be kept away from paper stocks until the designation lapses.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-012 is a handwritten musical score on three loose sheets of aged manuscript paper. The notation is written in a deep red ink that has never been identified. The final bars are blank.

SCP-012 is inert unless it is held in either hand, or seen through glass or an open door from within roughly 8 m. A subject exposed in either way sees red musical notation crowding the edges of their vision and hears faint, discordant notes. They grow steadily weaker for as long as the exposure lasts.

Each copy of SCP-012 carries its own degree of completion. Exposure advances it. Continuous exposure carries a blank copy to completion in a little over three minutes, and a subject left exposed for too long without rest may not survive it.

A subject exposed at the moment a copy is completed is designated SCP-012-2. Any paper that comes into the possession of SCP-012-2 is found, one sheet at a time, to have become a new blank copy of SCP-012. The designation lapses on the death of the subject.

page.title: Addendum 012-1: Test Log
text: Test 012-02: a researcher held SCP-012 for ten seconds. Faint notes were reported, and the subject was briefly unwell.
Test 012-05: SCP-012 was placed behind a glass front. Staff who stopped to look at it from close by were affected. Staff who walked past without looking were not.
Test 012-09: the glass front was replaced with a solid door. No further effects were reported while the door stayed shut.
Test 012-11: a researcher was exposed until a copy was completed. %rSubject redesignated SCP-012-2. Paper stocks in the wing were found replaced by blank scores.%r

page.title: Addendum 012-2: Provenance
page.text: SCP-012 has no recovery record. It was delivered to a reader of this file inside a sealed containment case, by the unidentified individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects. The individual warned the recipient never to hold the score, and never to keep it behind glass. See field notes.

jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp012_compositio: SCP-012 is an unfinished musical score written in red ink. It is harmless almost everywhere: in your inventory, in a chest, in a Sealed Containment Case, or behind the shut, solid door of a storage container.

It is dangerous in exactly two situations: while you hold it in either hand, and while you look at it in a storage container that stands open or has a glass front, from within 8 blocks. Red notes crowd your vision, you take damage every few seconds, and that copy's completeness meter climbs.

A copy fills from 0%% to 100%% in a little over three minutes of exposure. Whoever is exposed when it reaches 100%% becomes SCP-012-2 until they die: whenever paper enters their inventory, one sheet turns into a new blank SCP-012.
It cannot be crafted. Recover the SCP-012 dossier from an Archive Terminal and break its seal. A stranger in Foundation dress delivers it inside a Sealed Containment Case.
